A causal-discovery result

Source: R/cd-result.R
cd_result.Rd

The object returned by cd_discover() and cd_auto(). It holds the recovered graph as an adjacency matrix in the pcalg amat.cpdag convention, where graph[i, j] == 1 and graph[j, i] == 0 encodes the directed edge \(i \rightarrow j\), and graph[i, j] == graph[j, i] == 1 encodes an undirected (unoriented) edge \(i - j\).

Usage

cd_result(
  graph = numeric(0),
  method = NA_character_,
  method_name = "",
  family = NA_character_,
  language = "R",
  output = "cpdag",
  runtime_s = NA_real_,
  status = "ok",
  rationale = "",
  confidence = NA_character_,
  alternatives = list(),
  provenance = list()
)

Arguments

graph

A square numeric adjacency matrix in the amat.cpdag convention, with variable names as dimnames; empty when the method failed.

method

A single string: the identifier of the method that produced the result.

method_name

A single string: the human-readable method name.

family

A single string: the algorithm family (constraint, score, functional, continuous-optimisation, hybrid, or density).

language

A single string: the back-end language, "R" or "Python".

output

A single string: the native output type, one of "dag", "cpdag", or "pag".

runtime_s

A single number: wall-clock runtime in seconds.

status

A single string: "ok", or a short error description.

rationale

A single string: why the recommender chose this method.

confidence

A single string: "high", "moderate", or "low".

alternatives

A list of method labels the recommender considered as alternatives, in its preference order.

provenance

A list of call metadata (data characteristics, options).

Value

An S7 object of class cd_result.

Details

The rationale, confidence, and alternatives properties are populated by cd_auto() and are empty for a single-method cd_discover() call.

See also

Other results: cd_edges()

Examples

g <- matrix(c(0, 0, 1, 0), 2, 2,
            dimnames = list(c("x1", "x2"), c("x1", "x2")))
cd_result(graph = g, method = "pc_pcalg", method_name = "PC (Fisher-Z)")
#> <cd_result>: PC (Fisher-Z) [?, R]
#>   status    : ok
#>   variables : 2 (x1, x2)
#>   edges     : 1 directed, 0 undirected
